h: Yearning and Faithful Service Reveal the Full Divine Name

p: on which the decrees of the Torah hang,
It explains "My statutes" from the expression
"I have engraved a statute, I have decreed a decree"
(as they expounded in the Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma
רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת חֻקַּת, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה יט, א)
at the beginning of Parshas Chukas, Bamidbar Rabbah 19:1).
to which that statute is bound, etc."
In this parsha it is written,
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
and Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory, explained
that the Zohar refers to what is said
"a judgment of the God of Yaakov."
which is a matter without a reason,
is a matter with a reason
that there is a Torah she'b'al peh
which he originated from his own understanding,
and these are called halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai,
and the reason was not revealed to anyone
except Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
as a law without a reason
for which no reason need be given").
and he dealt with it generously
and the Gemara concludes, "rather, only the dialectic,"
meaning what he devised through his dialectic;
and of this the reason was not revealed
except that they arrive at it with ruach hakodesh
"This is the statute of the Torah":
"This is the decree of the Torah."
And about this they said in the Midrash
(רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה יט, ו; תַּנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת ח)
(Rabbah and Tanchuma, Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6; Tanchuma Chukas 8):
"To Moshe I reveal the reason of the Parah,
but for others it is a statute, etc."
and all the secrets of His house;
for this is the gift of his portion,
which was the aspect of the higher Shabbos.
"If you will walk in My statutes,"
placed right after what is said (Vayikra 26:2):
for at the onset of Shabbos
one attains the mystery of the servant.
this is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
as stated in the holy Zohar
the holiness of Atika Kadisha and Ze'ir Anpin.
to understand the reasons of the Torah,
"things that the Ancient of Days concealed"
and the mystery of one who searches the King's treasuries
and this is the totality of the holy Name";
in the holy Zohar (at the beginning of Parshas Behar):
"We have established this verse as referring to Knesses Yisrael,

p: whoever performs the commandments of the Torah
it is, as it were, as though he made Him above.
and therefore 'and you shall do them'
'and you shall make you' is written."
When it says "and they have explained it,"
the intention is to what they said in the Gemara
It is as though he made the words of Torah,
'And you shall keep, etc., and do them.'
It is as though he made himself,
as it says, 'and you shall do them';
כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד בֶּן חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹרָה כּוּלֵּי
"Whoever teaches his fellow's son Torah, etc.,"
since it expounds the pasuk "And you shall keep,"
to the keeping of the Torah and mitzvos in general:
he made the words of Torah.
And we have said that the matter is
but the daughters of Tzelofchad merited,
and it was written through them, etc."
And this is what it says in the parsha of the impure
what Hashem will command concerning you."
We have said that the term "stand"
since once its day has passed
but since he heard their cry,
from the depth of the heart,
and cry out, "Why should we be diminished?"
and through this I will merit
"and I will hear what Hashem will command concerning you."
And this is the meaning of
"We will do and we will hear";
that it is the language the ministering angels
to do the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
they will merit to hear the command of Hashem;
wants nothing of us but the heart,
And this is what they expounded in the Midrash Rabbah
If you have kept the Torah,
as though you had made them"
that is, the words of Torah,
(and as explained for Lag BaOmer, maamar 8).
And it appears that this is
as they said in the Midrash:
as though you had made yourselves, etc."
that the Gemara's intent too is,
as it were, about HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
just as the holy Zohar expounds;
with the derashah of the holy Zohar.
And about this the holy Zohar says:
"As though he made Me, and they have explained it";
and this expression is usual in the holy Zohar
in the revealed Midrashim of Chazal,

p: 'And David made a name, etc.' (Shmuel II 8:13)
as it were, he made a Name above;
and there was no king in the world
who merited this as David did,
who would rise at midnight, etc.,
until the holy Name rose onto the Throne
at the hour when the light rose in the day;
as it were, he made a Name, etc."
Now this needs to be understood:
according to the words of the holy Zohar,
he made a Name, as it were;
so why was this pasuk written specifically,
when he returned from smiting Aram, etc."?
the intent of the holy Zohar,
"until the holy Name rose onto the Throne,"
is that the meaning is not
the final heh of the Name Havayah,
as would appear at first glance
'And the son of the woman pronounced, etc.,'"
and as stated in the holy Zohar
"He took the heh of the holy Name, etc.";
and so too "Hashem and His Name are one" (Zechariah 14:9):
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קלד, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)
"until the holy Name rose onto the Throne"
"When I call out the Name of Hashem, etc."
that he separated the final heh from the Name,
And so here the meaning of
"until the holy Name rose onto the Throne"
the aleph pierced through the darkness
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב נד, א)
And this means that Kesser Elyon
saying, "Hashem shall reign forever and ever" (Shemos 15:18),
He is crowned with Kesser Elyon.
and the Ancient of Days sat."
And this is what it says:
"until the holy Name rose onto the Throne"
together with the upper tip of the yud,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סה, ב)
That is: David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
and accept the yoke of His kingship
when the light of day rose;
as it were, he made an actual Name,
(and so it appears from the commentary Mikdash Melech);
no thought can grasp anything at all,
that one can attain of Him, may His Name be blessed.
but that it should be permanent,
he can measure in his heart
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב שָׁם (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ח, יד)
And afterward it is written there (Shmuel II 8:14):
and all Edom became servants to David";
to judge the mountain of Esav,
and the kingship shall be Hashem's";
Hashem shall be One and His Name One"
the union of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah,
although this pasuk was already written
it is written a second time,
for this was the essential salvation.
as it were, he made an actual Name,
in Klal Yisrael, as mentioned above.
וְכֵן כְּתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ח, טו)
And so it is written afterward (Shmuel II 8:15):
justice and righteousness for all his people."
as stated in the holy Zohar (III 113b)
for such is the order from Yisrael's side:
and afterward they draw down the union,
David HaMelech, peace be upon him:
And this is what it says:
And this is the intent of the holy Zohar
"There was no king in the world
who merited this as David did, etc.":
אַחַר פָּסוּק וַיַּעַשׂ דָּוִד שֵׁם וְגוֹ׳
after the pasuk "And David made a name, etc.":
And about this the holy Zohar says:
'and you shall make you' is written"
"If you will walk in My statutes
they will make the entire Name,
of Ze'ir Anpin and Atika Kadisha
which is the totality of the Name Havayah,
together with the upper tip of the yud,
